protocol.shape: Plain repeats, ONE invocation per state per run, each with its own --report-json and --output-dir.
protocol.why_not_stability_runs_flag: eval_detector/eval_parser accept --stability-runs N, and Task 5's original step 1 named it. It is NOT used, deliberately. --stability-runs executes all N observations inside a single invocation, i.e. one session, which defeats Task 5's blocker 2: July's finding was that 3 same-session runs agreed perfectly while a run separated by 24h differed by up to 9 elements. Five back-to-back observations would measure a falsely low variance. Plain repeats also let the sweep be split across days and are the shape paper/analysis/ already consumes.
protocol.why_one_invocation_per_state: Compute-budget rule 2. A mid-run throttle inside a six-state invocation once recorded five states as n_detected=0, recall=0.0 — which reads as a catastrophic result rather than an infrastructure failure.
protocol.day_split: Runs 1-3 on 2026-08-30, runs 4-5 on 2026-08-31, so BOTH suites have observations spanning more than one day. This is what blocker 2 requires; running one suite entirely on each day would not satisfy it.
protocol.\u26a0\ufe0f_day_split_honesty: Runs 1, 2 and 3 all executed back-to-back on the evening of 2026-08-30 local (22:54Z to ~01:00Z), so run 3 carries a 2026-08-31 UTC timestamp purely because it crossed UTC midnight. DO NOT present runs 1-3 as spanning two days: they are effectively one session, and blocker 2's whole point is that same-session runs understate variance (July: 3 same-session runs agreed perfectly while a 24h-separated run differed by up to 9 elements). The genuine temporal separation in this measurement comes from exactly two places: the frozen parser observation recorded 2026-08-29, and runs 4-5 planned for 2026-08-31. The DETECTOR suite therefore has NO cross-day observation until run 4 lands — its runs 1-3 are one session. State that plainly wherever the detector stability number is quoted.

instrument_caveats: Identity is the normalized TITLE (detector) / normalized indicator.name (parser). level, code, description, age_band, source_page and standard_id are COMPARED FIELDS and are never in the identity key. The predecessor instrument keyed on (code, title) and was therefore blind to exactly the malformed-code defect it existed to catch.

detector_sort_key was FIXED on review 2026-08-30: as first drafted it ordered within-identity occurrences by `level` and `code`, both fields under test, so a code drift reordered the occurrences and paired run A's element against a different element in run B. It now sorts on source_text and source_page only. Pinned by self-check (f), which FAILS against the old key.

A 0.000 rate at N=5 is NOT evidence of determinism. A defect firing in a minority of runs easily yields five clean observations; 10 of 20 cached KY parser runs fired the bare-code defect historically. Treat every rate here as a LOWER BOUND on variance.

compute_stability compares the MULTISET of each field's values within an identity group, NOT occurrence-i-to-occurrence-i after a sort. Changed 2026-08-30 on review. Reason, measured on the real CA parser output: 94 standards collapse to 33 distinct indicator names, and 32 occurrences are separated by NO combination of age_band, source_page and source_text -- CA prints the same foundation once per proficiency column, so the columns differ only in indicator.code, the field under test. Positional pairing there would have required sorting by a field under test, which does not mask a change but inflates it: one drifted code would report as two code disagreements plus spurious description/standard_id ones. Multiset comparison is order-insensitive, needs no tie-break, and is equivalent to direct comparison at multiplicity 1.
